chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Muhammad from Salih ibn Abi Hammad from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who narrated it from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

It was said to him, 'Indeed, a man married a young girl, and his wife nursed her, then another woman nursed her.' Ibn Shubrumah said, 'The girl and his two wives became prohibited to him.' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said, 'Ibn Shubrumah erred; the girl and the wife who nursed her first are prohibited to him. As for the second one, she is not prohibited to him because she nursed his daughter.'

And the jurisprudence of this hadith is that when the first wife nurses the girl, the girl becomes prohibited to him because she becomes his daughter, and the second wife becomes prohibited to him because she is the mother of his wife. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'What is prohibited by lineage is also prohibited by nursing.' So when the last woman nurses her, she nurses her while she is the man's daughter, not his wife, so she is not prohibited to him for that reason. And it is not permissible for a free man to marry more than four free women. Allah the Exalted said, 'Marry those that are lawful to you of women, two or three or four.' The 'waw' here means 'or' without dispute. And whenever a man has four wives and divorces one of them, it is not permissible for him to contract marriage on another until the waiting period of the divorced woman has expired.

key_terms.ابْنُ شُبْرُمَةَ: Ibn Shubrumah (a jurist whose opinion was corrected)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific conditions under which a second nurse becomes prohibited to a man in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* refutes Ibn Shubrumah’s opinion by clarifying that the second nurse is not prohibited because she becomes the nurse of the man's daughter, not his wife, thereby illustrating the precise application of *radha'* (nursing kinship). It reinforces the principle that nursing prohibitions mirror lineage prohibitions and contextualizes the limit of four wives by specifying that a new marriage contract cannot be finalized until the *iddah* of the divorced wife has expired.
